title: Cu-modified ZnO nanostructures on 3D-printed photopolymer scaffolds for reusable photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue
content: Cu-modified ZnO nanostructures were hydrothermally grown on three-dimensional epoxy/acrylate photopolymer scaffolds fabricated by LCD-based vat photopolymerization. After surface activation and ZnO seed-layer deposition, coatings with nominal Cu contents of 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% were grown at 90 °C for 4 h. X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy confirmed preservation of hexagonal wurtzite ZnO, while Cu addition modified the principal diffraction reflections without detectable secondary Cu-containing crystalline phases. Electron microscopy and elemental analysis revealed dense rod-like nanostructures with Cu-dependent morphology and verified Cu in the coatings. Optical measurements showed Cu-dependent changes in reflectance, band-gap energy, and defect-related emission. After 180 min under artificial sunlight, the mean methylene blue (MB) degradation efficiency increased from (54.59 ± 1.61)% for ZnO/P to (83.67 ± 1.08)% for 2Cu–ZnO/P. The latter exhibited an apparent rate constant of (8.78 ± 0.39) × 10−3 min−1, approximately 2.2 times that of ZnO/P. Scavenger experiments indicated a predominant role of superoxide radicals under the investigated conditions. One of the three 2Cu–ZnO/P scaffolds was used for four additional cycles. Its MB degradation efficiency decreased from 84.88% in cycle 1 to 78.11% in cycle 5, corresponding to 92.02% retention of its first-cycle efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of Cu-modified ZnO on open cubic vertex-centroid scaffolds as reusable immobilized photocatalysts, with the lattice supporting coating growth and enabling recovery and reuse as a single structure.
